What comes up in St Marys

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table describes how these jobs generally go in this area. Your block may not match it, which is the reason for looking at it first.

Warehouse with slab and hardstand

On an industrial site there is frequently more concrete than building.

How it is handled
Structure removed first, then the slab and hardstand broken out and crushed so clean concrete is reused rather than landfilled.
What does it
Large excavator with a shear or grapple, hydraulic hammer, truck and dogs.

Post-war house on a regular block

The residential half of the work, consistent enough that the programme is predictable.

How it is handled
Bonded material removed under licence and cleared, then the structure down in one run and the block left level.
What does it
Midi excavator with a grapple, sized to the side gap.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

St Marys

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Residential and industrial side by side Factory and warehouse work a short distance from ordinary knockdowns, with very different surveys and waste streams.
  • Post-war housing on regular blocks Consistent stock, almost all of it pre 1990.
  • Unknown fill on older industrial land Worth testing before a dig is priced rather than after.
  • Good truck access on the industrial streets Built for heavy vehicles, which helps the cartage.

The industrial parts of St Marys are set up for trucks, so cartage is rarely the constraint there. On the residential side the usual side access limits apply and the side gap decides the machine.

St Marys questions

What people ask before we start

Do you demolish factories and warehouses?
Yes. It is licensed work and it runs as a sequence: hazardous materials survey, service disconnections, soft strip, then the structure, with steel and clean concrete separated as it comes down.
What happens to the slab and the hardstand?
Both can come out and both are recyclable. Clean concrete is crushed and reused rather than landfilled, which is usually the cheaper outcome as well as the better one.
How much does the haul to disposal add out here?
Enough to matter. The destination is set by the classification rather than by distance, so the classification is done properly and the cartage is priced on the real haul rather than an assumption.
Who signs off that the asbestos is gone?
An independent licensed assessor, not the removalist and not us. Max holds demolition licence AD214737, the removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the clearance is arranged as part of the same job.
